question: Can archived plasma samples from prior transdermal/topical CBD bioequivalence or PK studies (Zamarripa 2024 cohort, Heussler 2019 Fragile X cohort, other published transdermal product PK work) be re-assayed for the 7-COOH-CBD / 7-OH-CBD / parent CBD metabolite fingerprint with paired or proximal LFT data, sufficient to publish a first-pass test of the route-of-metabolism vs liver-safety hypothesis?
context: The reference document landed today identifies the metabolite-fingerprint + LFT pairing in transdermal vs oral CBD users as the specific missing measurement that would discriminate among three candidate mechanisms for the apparent transdermal hepatic safety advantage: (a) metabolite-pathway bypass, (b) lower systemic exposure overall, (c) some other route-specific factor. Building this study from scratch requires recruitment, IRB, blood draws — substantial cost and time. Re-assaying archived plasma is potentially much cheaper. Open questions: (i) which cohorts have archived plasma with consent terms permitting re-analysis for cannabinoid metabolites; (ii) what was the sample storage condition and is 7-COOH-CBD stable at -80C for 2-7 years (literature suggests yes, but should be verified per cohort); (iii) were LFTs measured at any timepoint in those cohorts and if so, can they be paired retrospectively; (iv) could a small new-recruitment study supplement an archived re-assay if archived data is partial. Worth pursuing as a methodological-feasibility question before committing to a prospective design. Document archive_id 9281572314dcb1a557a7177052d40721bddceac85132d177b491ea2a65399631.
